paper_metadata.title: Eutectic MoNbTa(WC)x Composites with Excellent Elevated Temperature Strength

evidence.quote: To develop materials with a promising utilization future in the extreme environments of aerospace, the MoNbTa(WC)x composites were prepared by vacuum arc melting, of which the crystal structure, microstructure, and compression properties at elevated temperature were investigated.
The strengthening mechanism of MoNbTa(WC) was mainly second-phase strengthening and boundary strengthening.

The composites with a nominal composition of MoNbTa(WC)x (x = 0.7 and 0.9 in a molar ratio, denoted as W0.7 and W0.9, respectively), were prepared by arc melting under a pure argon atmosphere on a water-cooled copper plate.

MoNbTa(WC)0.9 exhibited ultra-high true yield strength above 1.3 GPa and true fracture strain over 29% at 1200 ◦C.
MoNbTa(WC)0.9 exhibited ultra-high true yield strength above 1.3 GPa and true fracture strain over 29% at 1200 ◦C.

The synergetic enhancement of strength and ductility was achieved when the temperature was raised from 800 ◦C to 1200 ◦C, and the improvement range was larger in W0.9, which was due to C doping and solid solution strengthening.

The outstanding hyperthermal mechanical properties of W0.7 and W0.9 were mainly attributed to precipitation strengthening and edge dislocation-mediated enhancement coming from atom size mismatch, which was unaffected by high temperature.
With the doping of C with a small atom size, the stacking fault energy was decreased, and the dynamic recovery was restrained, resulting in a high strain hardening rate.
